description: Observed-order-of-accuracy sweep for grids/cartesian_uniform_1d/rules/ppm_D_periodic (Piecewise Parabolic Method, Colella-Woodward 1984, semi-discrete method-of-lines flux) driven by problems/advection_1d_ppm_periodic.esm, loaded once per resolution with the loader-API metaparameter binding (esm-spec 9.7.6 binding site 4). Exact solution sin(2 pi (x - c t)). HONEST ORDER: PPM is nominally 3rd order (parabolic reconstruction) and the UNLIMITED flux-difference is exactly the 4th-order central first derivative, but the original 1984 monotonicity limiter still clips the two smooth extrema of the sine (the classic smooth-extremum clipping of the CW84 limiter, cured only by later extremum-preserving variants), flattening the parabola there to first order. The global error is therefore dominated by two isolated first-order points, giving a sub-nominal, norm-dependent observed order -- the Julia golden gives median observed order 1.68 in L2 (pairwise 1.93, 1.66, 1.68) and 1.35 in Linf (pairwise 1.53, 1.35, 1.18). expected_order 1.5 with order_tolerance 0.25 brackets BOTH norm medians honestly (deviation 0.18 in L2, 0.15 in Linf); this is NOT a claim of 3rd-order convergence (which the CW84 limiter forecloses on any smooth periodic profile, whose extrema always trigger the clip). Conservation is exact and is gated separately by the problem's mean assertion.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator

blocked_upstream_bindings.rust: Rust hangs at every tolerance tried (loosest reltol 1e-6; all three solvers Erk/Bdf/Sdirk wedge). earthsci-toolkit-rs's diffsol integrator has no dtmin/max-step fail-fast guard, so on this stiff / non-smooth-min-max / large-AST RHS it drives dt->0 without terminating instead of erroring. Julia (Tsit5) and Python (LSODA) solve it. Remove once the Rust solver gains a step guard.
